photos.album: MenloPark
photos.description:
2994 Loveland Post Office (c. 1900) - Jane Loveland was appointed to her position by Senator Leland Stanford. She was the state's first lady postmaster. The building (constructed in 1892) was on Golder Lane, near the railroad depot, now Santa Cruz Ave. Loveland, who was given the building when she retired, moved it a few blocks west and converted it into her residence. In the photo to the right is the Palace Market meat wagon.
Hayden #S-123-1

photos.description: img211 - Google Map of the area south of SLAC overlayed with the map of Searsville from Drothy F. Regnery, The History of Jasper Ridge (c. 1991), p. 97. The scaling is dominated by matching the Mayfield-Searsville Road on Regnery’s map to Sand Hill Road on the Google map. Dennis Martin’s Lane (sometimes called Church Lane), which is seen to cut through SLAC at Sector 16, conforms to today’s Ansel Lane. The old Jane Goodale Primate Center is on Ansel Lane near what is marked on the map as House 2. There is still a gate at the SLAC perimeter fence where Ansel Lane meets the SLAC Klystron Gallery south road. Nothing remains of Dennis Martin’s Lane north of SLAC.

info.title: Cooper House - 110 Cooper Street: From the corner of Cooper Street and Pacific Avenue in Santa Cruz, CA
info.description: From Back: "Fine contemporary arts, crafts, imports, gourmet food and cocktails at Cooper House, the colorful and charming restoration of an 1895 court house."
info.rights: This postcard is the property of the Santa Cruz Public Libraries, California.
info.how_location_was_determined: The card shows the Cooper House (the restored 1895 Santa Cruz County Courthouse) at 110 Cooper Street at the corner of Pacific Avenue and Cooper Street.
info.how_year_was_determined: The 1895 courthouse was converted into the Cooper House retail and restaurant complex in 1972, and this H. S. Crocker Mirro-Krome card with a five-digit ZIP code dates to the 1970s.
